reactnative.title: React Native
reactnative.cmd.toggle: Show or hide the React Native panel
reactnative.none: No React Native or Expo project in this workspace
reactnative.blocked: Starting processes is off in read-only mode. Turn on "Allow processes" in Settings > Safety for this session.
reactnative.pods.hint: The iOS app will not build until the Pods are installed. Ask the agent to run "npx pod-install" in the project (with {pm} installed), or run it yourself in the Terminal.
reactnative.metro.title: Metro
reactnative.metro.noScript: package.json has no script that starts Metro. Add "start": "expo start" (Expo) or "start": "react-native start".
reactnative.devices.title: Devices
reactnative.devices.noIos: No iOS simulator found. Create one in Xcode > Window > Devices and Simulators.
reactnative.devices.noAndroid: No emulator or device found. Create an emulator in Android Studio (Device Manager) or plug in a phone with USB debugging on.
reactnative.devices.note: A device tool did not answer properly ({note}). The list may be incomplete.
reactnative.hint.xcode: Install Xcode from the App Store, then run "xcode-select --install".
reactnative.hint.macOnly: iOS simulators need a Mac with Xcode.
reactnative.hint.androidPlatformTools: Install Android Studio (or the SDK platform-tools) and set ANDROID_HOME.
reactnative.hint.androidEmulator: Install the Android Emulator from Android Studio > SDK Manager > SDK Tools.
reactnative.adb.unauthorized: unauthorized: accept the USB debugging prompt on the phone
reactnative.adb.noPermissions: no permission to use this device
reactnative.device.noIosScript: package.json has no "ios" script (expo run:ios / react-native run-ios), so the app cannot be installed from here.
reactnative.device.noAndroidScript: package.json has no "android" script (expo run:android / react-native run-android), so the app cannot be installed from here.
reactnative.confirm.title: Build and install with {runner}?
reactnative.confirm.desc: This builds the native app and installs it on a simulator or device. It takes minutes and writes build files into the project. An agent can never start it; only you can.
reactnative.logs.title: Device logs
reactnative.logs.waiting: Waiting for the app to log something...
reactnative.logs.idle: Press Start to follow the log of the booted simulator or the connected device. Secrets are masked.
reactnative.logs.ended: The log stream ended (exit code {code}). Is a device running?
reactnative.errors.title: Errors found
reactnative.errors.noDialog: The New Run dialog could not be opened.
reactnative.err.redbox.title: Red screen: the app stopped on an error
reactnative.err.redbox.why: The app code broke a rule React Native checks (for example a component was not registered or used wrongly). The message under the red screen says which.
reactnative.err.unresolvedModule.title: A file or package cannot be found
reactnative.err.unresolvedModule.why: The code imports something Metro cannot find: a wrong path, a typo, or a package that is not installed. Install the package or fix the import.
reactnative.err.undefinedFunction.title: Something that does not exist was used
reactnative.err.undefinedFunction.why: The code calls a function or reads a value from something that is empty (undefined or null), often because data has not loaded yet or a name is misspelled.
reactnative.err.nativeCrash.title: The app crashed
reactnative.err.nativeCrash.why: The native part of the app crashed. Common causes: a native module that is not linked or installed, a mismatch between a package and the React Native version, or a bad native call.
reactnative.err.gradleFailed.title: The Android build failed
reactnative.err.gradleFailed.why: Gradle could not build the Android app. Typical causes: the Android SDK is missing or not set up, a dependency cannot be downloaded, or a Java version mismatch.
reactnative.err.xcodeFailed.title: The iOS build failed
reactnative.err.xcodeFailed.why: Xcode could not build the iOS app. Typical causes: Pods not installed or out of date, a signing or provisioning problem, or a native code error.
reactnative.err.noBundleUrl.title: The app cannot reach Metro
reactnative.err.noBundleUrl.why: The app started but found no JavaScript bundle to load. Start Metro (the dev server) and make sure the device and your computer are on the same network.
reactnative.err.portInUse.title: The Metro port is already in use
reactnative.err.portInUse.why: Another program, often an older Metro still running, is using the port. Stop it, or let Metro use another port.
reactnative.err.podsOutOfDate.title: The iOS Pods are out of date
reactnative.err.podsOutOfDate.why: The installed Pods do not match Podfile.lock, usually after a package changed. Run "npx pod-install" in the project and build again.
reactnative.err.jsException.title: A JavaScript error
reactnative.err.jsException.why: The app code raised an error while running. The line below says what and where.
reactnative.toast.shutdown: Could not shut the device down
reactnative.section.name: React Native
reactnative.section.title: React Native
reactnative.section.desc: A panel for React Native and Expo apps: Metro, simulators and emulators, device logs and plain-language error cards. It only appears when a project of that kind is in the workspace.
reactnative.section.enableDesc: Nothing starts by itself. Metro and builds are started from the panel, with the same safety rules as the Run panel.
reactnative.refresh: Look for the project, the devices and the tools again
